decisions.reason: False positive: the complete cited Poincare proof, steps 2.1–3.1, explicitly obtains C(p)=1, although its Statement permits an unspecified C(p). On (0,1) this licenses ||z||2<=||z'||2 and coercivity 1/2. Independently recomputed a(v,w)=1, a(w,w)=4, Rv=w/4 and the nonlinear pairings 1/2 and 2/3. Countable Choice supplies the stated real H0^1 evolution triple; the quadratic supplier is scaled by 2. No item or interface repair is warranted.

False positive: SCHEMA.md explicitly requires a justified_by target to depend on the definition through deps. This is a discharge edge, not a cyclic premise: the definition specifies flux hypotheses and the theorem proves finite-dimensional test-coordinate continuity from Caratheodory continuity, growth and dominated convergence in step 1.1. The definition's Remarks independently establish A(v) in V* by componentwise measurable composition, (p-1)p'=p and Holder. The solution clause defines a class and assumes a continuous representative; it makes no existence assertion. The strict Sobolev range, common exceptional set and declared AC remain sound.

Confirmed nonfatal local proof/citation gap: F2 attributes derivative commutation and smooth V-valued differentiation to a supplier that proves only convolution convergence. Step 1.1 now differentiates kernel integrals using uniform difference-quotient error times ||u||L1(V), then tests the defining distribution identity with rho_epsilon(t-r) to establish Ji(dot u_epsilon)=rho_epsilon*u_prime. Applying the convergence supplier separately in V and V* proves both strong limits. Reviewed the uniform H Cauchy estimate, Holder passage and good-time endpoint estimate: delta^(1/p)||u(s_delta)||V <= 2^(1/p)||u||Lp(0,delta;V), so the endpoint oscillation vanishes for every p>1. Statement and all choice assumptions are preserved; no new prerequisite is needed.

Confirmed nonfatal convention/citation defect: the supplier introduces the scalar-test equation only under conjugate Lp-prime membership, whereas this theorem allows q<p-prime. F2 now states the equation explicitly for g in the theorem’s Lq(V*) space and explains that finite-time L1 bounds make both sides meaningful. This is the same distributional derivative convention and preserves every stated p,q case. Reviewed the proof: finite-dimensional H projections have epsilon||v||V remainders; coefficients are W11 with uniformly Lq derivatives, hence have a common positive Holder modulus (Lipschitz for q=infinity). Finite-grid interpolation gives total boundedness; completeness gives compactness; the uniform H bound gives convergence of the same subsequence in every finite Lr. No statement, supplier or page change is needed.

Confirmed nonfatal typing defect: J has domain H while the fixed vector v belongs to V. F1 and proof step 2.1 now consistently use J(iv); scalar integration by parts verifies the pivot weak derivative, and <J(iv),v>=||iv||H^2>0 verifies its nonzero norm. Direct period integration gives n-independent Lp(V) norms, sine orthogonality gives squared separation T||iv||H^2, and the cosine derivative norm is a positive constant times n for all 1<=q<=infinity. The Statement is unchanged and no downstream propagation is triggered.
